name: Naboth
source_summary: A Jezreelite who refused to sell his ancestral vineyard to King Ahab out of faithfulness to God's covenant law on inherited land, and was murdered on false charges arranged by Jezebel as a result.
family_friendly_summary: Naboth owned a vineyard right next to King Ahab's palace in Jezreel, land that had belonged to his family for generations. When Ahab offered to buy it or trade for a better one, Naboth refused, because God's law taught that family land was meant to stay within a family from generation to generation, not be casually sold away. Ahab sulked over being refused, and his wife Jezebel decided to take matters into her own hands. She arranged for false witnesses to accuse Naboth of a crime he never committed, and he was killed as a result, allowing Ahab to simply take the vineyard. God saw this terrible injustice and sent the prophet Elijah to confront Ahab and Jezebel directly, promising that they would eventually face serious consequences for what they had done to Naboth.
adult_story: Naboth owned a vineyard in Jezreel adjacent to King Ahab's palace, and when Ahab offered to buy it or exchange it for a better vineyard, Naboth refused: "the LORD forbid me that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers" (1 Kings 21:1-3) -- a direct appeal to the law's protection of ancestral land within Israel's tribes (compare Leviticus 25:23; Numbers 36:7). Ahab went home and sulked, refusing to eat, until Jezebel took matters into her own hands: she wrote letters in Ahab's name and seal, instructing the elders of Jezreel to proclaim a fast, seat Naboth prominently, and have two worthless men falsely accuse him of cursing God and the king, a capital crime under the law they cynically manipulated (21:4-10). The elders complied, and Naboth was stoned to death on the false charge; Jezebel then told Ahab to go take possession of the vineyard, since Naboth was dead (21:11-16). God did not let the injustice pass unnoticed: He sent Elijah to confront Ahab at the very vineyard, pronouncing that dogs would lick Ahab's blood where they had licked Naboth's, and that judgment would fall on Jezebel and his entire house for the murder (21:17-24). Naboth's death, an innocent man judicially murdered for refusing to surrender his God-given inheritance, stands as one of Scripture's starkest indictments of royal power abused against the powerless.

devotionals: Naboth was murdered on false charges by corrupt power that wanted what he wouldn't give up. Jesus was condemned the same unjust way, an innocent man falsely accused.
God would not let Naboth's innocent blood go unanswered. Jesus's innocent blood went further still — shed not just to be avenged, but to save us.
